protocol.input: 16 normalized public features and explicit selected action in {0,1,2}
protocol.model: 16-dimensional fixed recurrent state, deterministic fixed projection/recurrence, online-trained linear readout
protocol.limitations: initial reservoir/state-space comparator; fixed recurrence, not a tuned/trainable full RNN or Bayesian/model-based learner

interpretation.state_size: Recurrent serialized state is 3,170 bytes vs MR32 3,853 bytes; recurrent Python object estimate 5,808 vs MR32 7,335 bytes.
interpretation.runtime: Recurrent wall time is noisy and differs by runner: 0.118s Windows / 0.103s Ubuntu vs MR32 0.102s Windows / 0.074s Ubuntu. In these runs the recurrent comparator is not faster than MR32. It is faster or slower? No robust conclusion; repeat controlled timing required.
interpretation.peak: Recurrent traced peak ~114.6KB vs MR32 ~178.4KB, but this is not process RSS.
interpretation.decision: No scientific winner. This is an initial comparator and not a controlled parity benchmark. The comparison demonstrates MR32 is not obviously more compact than a simple recurrent state-space representation.

limits: Single deterministic synthetic stream and one 256-step inventory per OS.
Hosted runners are not calibrated benchmark hardware; timing is noisy.
tracemalloc is not OS RSS; Python object deep-size is interpreter-dependent.
Persistence envelopes and semantics are not common across implementations.
No trained recurrent optimization sweep or Bayesian/model-based comparator.
No prediction-error efficacy, reward, decision gain, causal correction advantage or unfamiliar transfer measured.
decision: A simple recurrent-state control is now in the suite. MR32 does not show a compactness advantage; inference/runtime results are inconclusive/noisy. Next: common checkpoint envelope, controlled repeated timing/resource measurement, and a proper Bayesian control. No original-world admission or scientific claim.
